title: priv-controlplane: Terraform lifecycle orchestration, automated state migrations, and proactive health reporting for EKS
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Scope: author a new reusable Terraform module 'priv-controlplane' to provision and operate Redwood Private EKS control planes with built-in lifecycle hooks, automated state migration helpers, and proactive health reporters. The module must be idempotent, support immutable roll-forward naming for minimal blast radius, and expose observability outputs consumed by Redwood Console.

Goals:
- Replace ad-hoc control-plane provisioning scripts with a single opinionated module.
- Automate migration of legacy TF state (scripts + docs) for customers upgrading from older 'eks-provisioner' modules.
- Add deploy-time and runtime health reporters (CloudWatch metrics + consolidated /health endpoint) to detect control-plane drift and failed upgrades.
- Provide upgrade guard rails: preflight checks, canary nodegroups, and safe rollback paths.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use terraform 1.5+ and aws provider 5.x to leverage resource-level plan detection; requires bumping infra CI images. Trade-off: developer churn updating local dev images.
- Choose immutable name suffixes (yyyyMMdd-HHMM) on ASG/nodegroup resources during upgrades to enable quick rollback by reattaching previous autoscaling groups. Trade-off: temporary double allocation during canary rollouts; mitigated by configurable burst_capacity and tagging.
- State migration strategy: provide a bin/states-migrate.sh helper that runs a documented sequence of 'terraform state mv' and 'terraform import' for identified legacy resources. This avoids writing provider-specific refactors into the module. Trade-off: manual steps required for some custom customer infra; documented in Confluence guide.
- Health reporting: export CloudWatch CustomMetrics (ControlPlaneUpgradeProgress, ControlPlaneDriftDetected, LastSuccessfulUpgrade) and a lightweight Lambda that pings the EKS control plane and writes a consolidated /health object to S3 for Redwood Console ingestion. Trade-off: additional AWS resources and cost, but provides strong SLA evidence for Dedicated/Private customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module exposes inputs for cluster_name, eks_version, kms_key_arn, private_subnet_ids, control_plane_tags, upgrade_strategy (immediate|canary|manual), burst_capacity, and observability_topic_arn.
- PR with module code merged and accompanied by unit-style terratest that runs create-destroy against a small scratch account (or mock provider) in CI.
- State migration script verified against a copy of legacy state in QA and documented in Confluence (link below).
- Health metrics emitted and visible in Console demo dashboard (end-to-end).
- Security review completed and KMS cross-account usage approved.

Non-goals:
- Not responsible for worker node image pipelines (separate module).
- Not implementing full operator; this is a Terraform-first provisioning pattern with lightweight runtime reporters only.

implementation_steps: Create module skeleton with documented inputs/outputs and examples/README.md
Implement control-plane provisioning resources: aws_eks_cluster (control plane config), aws_eks_addon where applicable, IAM roles, KMS key bindings
Add optional immutable naming suffix and upgrade_strategy logic via locals
Add CloudWatch metrics + Lambda health reporter resources and IAM policies
Write state migration helper script with safe checks and dry-run mode
Add terratest/unit tests and CI job (mock/localstack for speed), validate provider versions
Run canary deploy in QA account and exercise rollback flow; capture metrics
Open security review and remediate any KMS/privilege concerns
Document runbook (upgrade, rollback, migration) in Confluence and link in module README
